tasks.text: Open the renewal file in the agency management system and confirm expiring terms, carriers, and premiums.
Send the internal renewal kickoff note with team assignments, renewal date, and target dates.
Confirm the service team for the renewal and record who owns each line of coverage.
Review the Exempt Commercial Purchaser (ECP) form and confirm it is current for any surplus lines placement.
Confirm the surplus lines home state assignment for the coming term and notify the placement contact.
Schedule the Internal Strategy Meeting (ISM) and circulate an agenda covering client goals and known changes.
Build the ISM deck from the prior-year version, refreshed for current exposures and market conditions.
Request loss runs from each incumbent carrier and build a loss summary by line.
Send the client an exposure update request with prior-year schedules prefilled.
Pull benchmarking and market condition data for the client's industry and program size.
Draft the renewal strategy document: loss summary, exposure changes, and program options.
Review and approve the strategy document before it goes to the client.
Hold the renewal strategy meeting with the client and agree on the market approach.
Confirm target terms, pricing expectations, and the list of markets to approach.
Send a written recap covering agreed strategy, assignments, and target dates.
Review returned exposure data for completeness and follow up on gaps.
Complete ACORD applications and supplemental forms for each line being marketed.
Refresh loss runs if the valuation date will be stale by the time quotes are due.
Assemble the submission package and route it to the AE for review.
Approve the submission and share it with the client before release.
Release the submission to the market with a stated quote due date and track receipt.
Log quotes as they arrive and chase markets that have not responded by the due date.
Route underwriter questions to the client team and return the answers to the market.
Build the Cost & Coverage Comparison (CCC) against expiring terms and flag gaps, new exclusions, and changed sublimits.
Negotiate pricing, terms, and conditions with the preferred markets.
Finalize the proposal, including compensation disclosure, and present it to the client.
Offer premium finance options where the client wants to spread payment.
Obtain written bind instructions from the client before the expiration date.
Issue bind orders to the selected carriers and confirm receipt.
Check binders against the quoted terms and request corrections in writing.
Send the client the binders, a binder transmittal letter, and the list of open subjectivities.
Update the agency management system and the certificate system with the bound policy terms.
Collect signed applications, surplus lines forms, and any other carrier-required signatures.
Confirm bound premium, taxes, fees, and surplus lines charges against the binder.
Agree the premium allocation across entities or locations with the client.
Issue the invoice and record the payment terms and due date.
Reconcile carrier invoices to the binder and resolve differences before they age.
Track payment and follow up ahead of any cancellation or audit deadline.
Meet internally to list open subjectivities, service commitments, and their owners.
Close carrier subjectivities and keep written evidence in the document management system.
Issue updated certificates and auto ID cards from the certificate system.
Produce the program summary and schedule of insurance for the bound term.
Track policy receipt and follow up with carriers that are late.
Check issued policies against the binder and request correcting endorsements.
Deliver the policies with a policy transmittal letter (PTL) and file the final set in the document management system.
